name: Celery
lede: Celery is a pale, yellow-green named for the vegetable's pale inner stalks rather than its greener outer ribs.

sections.title: The pale stalk, not the whole plant
sections.body:
The name comes from the vegetable [[celery]], whose outer stalks run a deeper green while the blanched inner heart stays close to this pale, lime-tinted shade [1]. Our library finds this exact cluster recorded only by the 2010 xkcd color survey, with no CSS, Wikipedia, or dictionary entry of the same name [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[light-pea-green]], [[very-light-green]] and [[celery]], at 3, 4.2 and 4.2 ΔE [1]. Siblings in the same yellow-green range are [[chartreuse]], [[lime]], and [[mint]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this pale yellow-green covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. The combination of near-white lightness and strong chroma this color needs is rare in aged oil paint, where pale greens tend to have drifted toward grey over centuries of varnish [2].
